_readme: One entry per body system. To add a system: add its territories, its game connections, which Recall Rx topics and Loops belong to it, and the wording rules that tag a card to a territory. Then run tools/build_bank.py --system <id>. Every anatomical statement in 'connections' is shown to players, so it must be true.

connections.note: The plasma membrane encloses the cytoplasm and its organelles.
The nuclear envelope is continuous with the rough endoplasmic reticulum.
Cell junctions in the plasma membrane hold epithelial cells together.
Epithelium rests on connective tissue at the basement membrane.
Connective tissue sheaths wrap muscle fibers (endomysium, perimysium, epimysium).
Connective tissue sheaths wrap nerve fibers (endoneurium, perineurium, epineurium).
Motor neurons signal skeletal muscle fibers at the neuromuscular junction.

linkLabels.pathway: One opens into or grows from the other

connections.note: Dermal papillae interlock with the epidermis.
The reticular layer of the dermis sits on the hypodermis.
A hair follicle is a downgrowth of the epidermis.
The follicle and its arrector pili muscle sit in the dermis.
Sebaceous glands open into hair follicles.
Sweat gland coils sit in the deep dermis.
The nail plate is made by epidermal cells of the nail matrix.

connections.note: The occipital condyles sit on the atlas (C1).
The ribs articulate with the thoracic vertebrae.
The clavicle meets the sternum at the sternoclavicular joint.
The humerus meets the scapula at the shoulder joint.
The sacrum meets the hip bones at the sacroiliac joints.
The femur meets the hip bone at the hip joint.

linkLabels.border: Muscles cross from one region to the next

connections.note: The trapezius runs from the neck onto the shoulder and back.
The deltoid and rotator cuff muscles cross the shoulder joint onto the humerus.
Biceps brachii and brachialis cross the elbow to the radius and ulna.
Forearm flexor and extensor tendons cross the wrist into the hand.
The external oblique arises from the lower ribs.
The inguinal ligament marks where the abdominal wall meets the thigh.
The quadriceps and hamstrings cross the knee to the tibia and fibula.
They meet at the central sulcus.
The lateral sulcus separates them.
They meet behind the end of the lateral sulcus.
They meet at the parieto-occipital sulcus.
They share a border on the lateral and inferior surfaces.
They face each other across the transverse fissure and tentorium cerebelli.
Thalamocortical fibers run between them (thalamic radiations).
Thalamocortical fibers run between them (thalamic radiations).
Thalamocortical fibers run between them (thalamic radiations).
Thalamocortical fibers run between them (thalamic radiations).
The hypothalamus sits directly below the thalamus.
The diencephalon is continuous with the midbrain.
The diencephalon is continuous with the midbrain.
The brainstem is continuous from midbrain to pons.
The brainstem is continuous from pons to medulla.
The medulla becomes the spinal cord at the foramen magnum.
The superior cerebellar peduncles join them.
The middle cerebellar peduncles join them.
The inferior cerebellar peduncles join them.

linkLabels.border: Physically joined, or parts of the same brain region
linkLabels.pathway: A hormone from one acts on the other

connections.note: The infundibulum joins the pituitary gland to the hypothalamus.
Both are parts of the diencephalon.
TSH from the anterior pituitary acts on the thyroid gland.
ACTH from the anterior pituitary acts on the adrenal cortex.
FSH and LH from the anterior pituitary act on the gonads.
Thyroid hormone feeds back on the hypothalamus.
Cortisol feeds back on the hypothalamus.
Sex steroids feed back on the hypothalamus.
Epinephrine from the adrenal medulla inhibits insulin release from the islets.

linkLabels.pathway: Blood flows from one to the other

connections.note: The venae cavae empty into the right atrium.
Blood passes through the tricuspid valve.
Blood leaves through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk.
The pulmonary veins return blood to the left atrium.
Blood passes through the mitral (bicuspid) valve.
Blood leaves through the aortic valve into the aorta.
Systemic capillary beds link the arteries to the veins.
The coronary arteries branch from the ascending aorta.
The coronary sinus empties into the right atrium.
The interatrial septum separates them.
The interventricular septum separates them.

linkLabels.border: Lymph flows from one to the other
linkLabels.pathway: Lymphocytes travel between them in the blood

connections.note: Afferent lymphatic vessels carry lymph into lymph nodes.
Efferent vessels drain toward the lymphatic trunks and ducts.
Lymph from the tonsils drains to cervical lymph nodes.
T cell precursors travel from red bone marrow to the thymus.
B cells made in red bone marrow travel in the blood to the spleen.
Mature T cells leave the thymus and settle in lymph nodes.
Mature T cells leave the thymus and settle in the spleen.

linkLabels.border: Air passes from one to the next, or the structures touch

connections.note: The nasal cavity opens into the nasopharynx.
The laryngopharynx opens into the larynx.
The trachea begins below the cricoid cartilage.
The trachea divides into the main bronchi at the carina.
The main bronchi enter the lungs at the hilum.
Terminal bronchioles lead to respiratory bronchioles and alveoli.
Alveoli fill most of the lung.
The base of each lung rests on the diaphragm.

linkLabels.border: Food passes from one to the next, or the organs are joined
linkLabels.pathway: A duct carries secretions between them

connections.note: Food passes from the mouth into the oropharynx.
The esophagus joins the stomach at the cardia.
The pyloric sphincter opens into the duodenum.
The ileum joins the cecum at the ileocecal valve.
The lesser omentum connects the liver to the stomach.
Bile reaches the duodenum through the bile duct.
The pancreatic duct empties into the duodenum.
The bile duct and the pancreatic duct join at the hepatopancreatic ampulla.

linkLabels.border: Urine passes from one to the next, or the structures touch

connections.note: Interlobar and arcuate arteries carry blood out to the cortex.
The renal vessels and the renal pelvis pass through the hilum together.
The cortex surrounds the renal pyramids of the medulla.
Renal papillae drain urine into the calyces.
The renal pelvis narrows into the ureter.
The ureters open into the bladder at the trigone.
The urethra leaves the bladder at the internal urethral orifice.

linkLabels.border: Sperm or egg passes from one to the next
linkLabels.pathway: Same embryonic origin (not joined in the body)

connections.note: Sperm leave the testis through the efferent ductules into the epididymis.
The ductus deferens joins the duct of the seminal gland to form the ejaculatory duct.
The ejaculatory ducts open into the prostatic urethra.
The fimbriae of the uterine tube sweep over the ovary.
The uterine tubes open into the uterus.
The cervix opens into the vagina.
Testes and ovaries are homologous gonads.
The penis and the clitoris develop from the same embryonic structure.
